message.reasoning:
No abstract present — deliverable requires ~150-word abstract. Also no figures. Word count seems under 1500. VW scandal misdescribed (diesel emissions, not crash-safety tests, "electric vehicles" wrong) — technical error. Recommendation contradicts conclusion somewhat (accept contract but delay launches). No abstract → structure criterion lower. References: 4, IEEE-ish, some incomplete (BBC no URL). Evidence quotes needed.

C1: intro identifies issues, stakeholders, org context — very good/excellent. Stakeholders yes, context yes. Give 8 (several issues, both context and stakeholders arguably present → could be 10; issues identified: quality vs business, harm, integrity — I'd say 8–10. Give 9? Levels only allow 10,8,6... whole number within range — ranges are single points except None 0. So choose 8 or 10. Both context and stakeholders demonstrated → 10? Issues: shipping defective products, professional integrity, trust. I'll give 8 since depth limited.

C2: balanced arguments for/against, conclusions for stakeholders — arguments decent depth, conclusion mostly company/Rachel. Give 8.

C3: structure logical, conclusion supported — mostly, but recommendation contradicts (accept contract then delay). Give 6? Arguments support conclusion reasonably; give 8? The recommendation inconsistency and abrupt "lose her job" broken paragraph. Give 6.

C4: references 4, case studies (NHS, VW), quantitative (1% of 5000). VW misdescribed. Give 8.

C5: no abstract, no figures, typos ("DICUSSION", "erosion ofprofessional"), broken citation formatting. Give 6.

Requirements: R1 partial (data loss vs physical harm discussed briefly), R2 yes, R3 partial (large-scale testing for future safety mentioned briefly), R4 yes, R5 yes, R6 partial (evidence but VW error, law not sole basis), R7 partial (recommendation contradictory). Abstract missing → deliverable partial.
